results.title: Preview: Ipswich Town v Arsenal
results.raw_content:
![Home](/images/logo.svg)

Highbury House

75 Drayton Park

London, N5 1BU

Our Carabao Cup campaign begins in the third round at Portman Road as we take on Ipswich Town on Tuesday, September 15, at 8pm (UK time).

The Tractor Boys overcame League One side Leicester City in the previous round to set up a clash with us for the first time in this competition since 2011, when we knocked Ipswich out in the semi-finals over two legs.

We reached the final of this competition last term, and as we gear up to do it all again, we're also looking to register a seventh-straight victory at the start of this campaign against the Premier League new boys.

## PROMOTION PROMISE

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/ca3810046fbd-london-england-leif-davis-of-ipswich-town-celebrates-scoring-his-teams-second-go.webp)

After celebrating promotion back to the top-flight for the first time in more than 20 years in 2024, Ipswich suffered relegation straight back to the Championship in 2024/25. The Tractor Boys bounced straight back up after finishing second last season, and there have been signs that this campaign will be different .

A dramatic late winner at home to Sunderland has been built upon with an enthralling 3-2 victory over 10-player Crystal Palace this weekend. Last time they were in the Premier League, Ipswich managed just four victories - their tally is already two after four matches.

Gary O'Neil has been tasked with keeping the Tractor Boys in the top-flight after replacing long-term manager Kieran McKenna this summer. The ex-Wolves boss can now turn his attention away from the Premier League and onto the League Cup, a competition they're yet to win in their history.

## WHAT THE MANAGERS SAY

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/7f8efaaa087a-sunderland-england-mikel-arteta-manager-of-arsenal-looks-on-during-the-premier-l.webp)

**Arteta:** “We'll look at the players' eyes and they will say they want to play, and ‘I want to win a game, and I want to improve.'

"They will review the [Sunderland] game, and they will be willing for more because I know the boys."

![Arteta: 'Our players are willing for more'](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/large_landscape/49edc31bbb34-london-colney-england-arsenal-manager-mikel-arteta-attends-a-press-conference-at.webp)
![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/c29c6834bbbd-manchester-england-gary-oneil-manager-of-ipswich-town-looks-on-before-the-premie.webp)

**O'Neil:**“Arsenal are tough to beat, even if you do everything right. I'll make some changes to my team, I'm sure Mikel will make changes to his team, but it's a game we want to win. I want to get as far in the cups as we can.

“We’re going to give it our best go at home under the lights. I think we missed the opportunity against Liverpool. We played well, but it was already 2-0. We missed the opportunity to use the energy of Portman Road under the lights against a big side."

## TEAM NEWS

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/734b4e054e15-sunderland-england-jurrien-timber-of-arsenal-takes-on-nilson-angulo-of-sunderlan.webp)

Jurrien Timber returned to the pitch for the second half in our win over Sunderland for the first time since the Champions League final in May. That was at the expense of Ben White, who was forced off at half-time due to an injury.

Cristhian Mosquera and William Saliba both missed the trip to the Stadium of Light as they continue to recover from their respective injuries.

As for our hosts, summer signing Emersonn came off in the 3-2 victory over Crystal Palace with a quad issue. However, O'Neil said the Brazilian striker was likely to be rested anyway for our trip.

The striker is one of just three injury concerns for the hosts alongside Jack Taylor, who has a knee injury, and Azor Matusiwa, who has a thigh issue but could still be fit to play. Zian Flemming, who featured for Burnley in an earlier round, is eligible to play due to a change in rules by the EFL.

![The best snaps before Carabao Cup trip to Ipswich](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/large_landscape/7030ede0db51-gallery-cover.webp)

## TALKING TACTICS

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/2bc507b59385-london-england-leif-davis-and-abdul-fatawu-of-ipswich-town-celebrate-after-the-p.webp)

*Adrian Clarke:*O’Neil is a flexible tactician who is prepared to switch formations game by game, but so far his side has exclusively started in a 4-2-3-1.Much will depend on how much they want to rotate, but one of their key strengths is the number of skilful attacking midfielders and wide players at O’Neil’s disposal, while left-back Leif Davis has enjoyed an outstanding start, scoring twice and registering an assist. If the 26-year-old starts, we will need to track his marauding runs, while his precise left foot also deserves respect.

O’Neil’s central midfield unit in Premier League games has been built around the industry of Sasa Lukic and Exequiel Palacios, who are both aggressive in their style. Ex-Burnley man Florentino could come in and do a similar job, but if he starts Marcelino Nunez it will point towards a slightly bolder approach in that department.

I would expect us to have over 55% possession, so the two most dangerous areas we need to watch are Ipswich’s direct attacks on the break (they've already had 8 shots from those in four league games) and their threat from high turnovers. Two of their Premier League strikes have come in that manner, so do not be surprised if they press us with a little hostility.  
  
  
  
However Ipswich have faced 26 league shots on target, a joint high in the division, leaking 10 goals in four outings. Caught a little open at times, they are not renowned for their compactness or solidity. With all this in mind, I expect a fairly open contest, with plenty of goalmouth action.

## FACTS AND STATS

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/5f84dccb3265-london-england-laurent-koscielny-celebrates-scoring-a-goal-for-arsenal-with-joha.webp)

Ipswich have lost 14 of their last 18 meetings with us in all competitions (W2 D2), including six of their last seven without scoring, with the other a 1-0 League Cup semi-final first leg win in 2010/11.

We have progressed from two of our three previous League Cup ties against Ipswich, the 1970/71 second round and 2010/11 semi-final, losing the other 2-1 in the 2000/01 third round.

The Tractor Boys have progressed from seven of their last nine third-round ties in the League Cup, most recently against Wolves in 2023/24.

We have progressed from 21 of our last 23 third-round ties in the League Cup, falling at this stage only in 2014/15 (v Southampton) and 2022/23 (v Brighton).

Gary O’Neil has lost all four of his managerial meetings with us in all competitions (one with Bournemouth, three with Wolves). Only against Manchester United and West Ham has he managed more games without ever avoiding defeat (both five).

## MATCH OFFICIALS

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/662ac9375924-bankes.webp)

Peter Bankes will be in charge, the third successive League Cup tie in which Bankes has refereed us. The 44-year-old took charge of our 1-0 victory over Chelsea in the semi-final second leg before also officiating the final against Manchester City.

There will be no VAR for our visit to Portman Road. This is because of the EFL ruling that VAR can be used only in rounds of the competition when every stadium hosting a match has access to the technology.

**Referee:**Peter Bankes  
  
**Assistants:**Constantine Hatzidakis, Alex James  
  
**Fourth official:** Josh Smith

## PORTMAN ROAD VISITS

Our last visit to Portman Road in the League Cup saw the hosts cause a massive shock in the semi-final first leg back in the 2010/11 season, as Tamas Priskin netted the only goal of the game for the then Championship side. But we turned things around in the second leg at Emirates Stadium, winning 3-0 to book our place at Wembley.

Our visits to Suffolk in the Premier League have been much happier. In 2024/25, we won 4-0 with two goals from Leandro Trossard, plus efforts from Gabriel Martinelli and Ethan Nwaneri. Our previous visit saw goals from Freddie Ljungberg and Thierry Henry help us win 2-0 in December 2001.

![From the vault: Five memorable wins at Ipswich](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/large_landscape/a4b709efafb8-campbell-goal-ipswich.webp)

## LIVE COVERAGE

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/c63db7811f57-lfn5ipswichpromo1920x1080.webp)

There will be live commentary of the game on [Arsenal.com](http://arsenal.com/) and The Arsenal app *(download now on [iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/the-arsenal-official-app/id332060637)/[Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.arsenal.official&hl=en_GB))*from just before kick-off, when Dan Roebuck and Adrian Clarke will be behind the mics guiding you through all the on-field action.

*You can also find out [which broadcasters are showing the action live](https://www.arsenal.com/news/how-to-watch-sunderland-v-arsenal-live-on-tv-aF3zA4H2Lo3t), wherever you are in the world.*

![How to watch Ipswich Town v Arsenal live on TV](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/large_landscape/7bbdd43c0374-ipswich-england-a-general-view-of-portman-road-during-the-during-the-pre-season.webp)![U21s preview: Leyton Orient v Arsenal](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/xl_landscape/03d41679dfa5-arsenaleflvertutrophyfixture16x9away.webp)

results.title: Every word of Renée's pre-Manchester United press ...
results.raw_content:
![Home](/images/logo.svg)

Highbury House

75 Drayton Park

London, N5 1BU

Renée Slegers was back in front of the media for her pre-Manchester United press conference at the Sobha Realty Training Centre on Thursday.

Our head coach shared the latest team news, looked ahead to our Emirates Stadium return and discussed the weekend’s opposition.

![Get your tickets for WSL clash with Man United!](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/large_landscape/6c0fa72cd011-gettyimages-2295072895.webp)

Here’s everything she had to say on the following subjects…

**on how we’ve tried to become more clinical in training this week:**  
  
The best thing is always to get back onto the grass and execute. I think psychologically that's good as well for everyone to be able to action things. So we've looked at some things. Of course, we were happy with our dominance in the game and our entries in the final third, entries in the box, amount of shots, but we've also been looking at how we can create even bigger opportunities for ourselves when the spaces are really tight and there's a lot of bodies in the box. So what are the moments in the game and how do we create spaces? We've applied some ideas, we've reviewed together with the players, we've been on the training page and the players' reaction has been really, really good. They've been working hard in training.

**on if having to leave senior players out of the squad is a good problem to have:**  
  
We have everyone in a great position. We have good fitness and we have a lot of quality and we think over time it's going to benefit us. We're also now going into short turnarounds with midweek Champions League games so we're going to need everyone as ready and as fresh as possible. We definitely think that on the long run, long term, this is really good for us.

**on if Cerci or Reuteler could feature this weekend:**  
  
They could. We have one more session left and then we're going to go through player readiness, different scenarios in the game, different qualities that we anticipate we need. Of course there's always a medical handover as well. They've come in and they're great players, both of them. They both have had disrupted pre-seasons, have been away from the team a couple of weeks and we just felt like it needed a little bit more time to get settled. But it's looking really good so far this week, they've been training really well.

**on Reid, Van Domselaar and Agyemang and if there are any more injuries:**  
  
We have one more injury picked up this week and that's Elisa de Almeida, so she won't be available.

![Gallery: Women’s team prepare for Man United](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/large_landscape/8755878f03c8-z923772i0t8yl2l.webp)

**on if United will come into this match with even more determination after their big defeat to Chelsea:**  
  
Of course, I can imagine they're not happy with the start of their season. They're going to come to the Emirates. Let's see what their plan is, how they're going to attack this game. I think what's important for us is that we have the focus on ourselves because we come away from Brighton, which was a good win in an away game at Crawley, but then of course we weren't satisfied and we were frustrated with the game against Palace at Emirates. So we are looking to do things better for ourselves. So there's a big focus on ourselves, but of course always respecting the opposition.

**on if this game will be more open than last season’s 0-0 draws with United:**  
  
I think they have a robust defending organisation. Normally that's what we've been facing when we've played against them. With the changes they've made, they've shown some different things. At the same time, I'm not sure how they're going to approach this game against us, what their focus will be in the game. But we'll know it will be a very competitive game against United on Saturday.

**on how difficult it is for a new manager to come in and implement their ideas quickly:**  
  
She [Eva Olid]'s obviously coming late in pre-season. If I look at the pre-season that we've had, we've had a lot of change in the squad. But how long it takes to make everyone aware of the game model, and how you connect with your teammates and how you really deeply understand each other almost without looking, that takes time. I understand the challenge that she has. As a coach, it's a decision to make. Are you going to go and change things straight away or are you going to have another approach where you progressively, over time, look to change things? That's probably the balance for her. I don't know what her philosophy is. I can imagine it's a challenge. Let's see what they do on Saturday against us.

**on the opportunity to go 20 matches unbeaten in the WSL:**  
  
It’s of course mixed emotions when I hear that stance, it’s very positive that we’re hard to beat and that’s what we feel about ourselves, but also with some recency bias as well of the last game against Crystal Palace where we weren’t able to score that goal, and didn’t get the win. It’s double, of course we’re proud, but at the same time there are some draws in there like the last one against Palace. When I put that with some of the draws we had last year, it’s different for me, if I look at the dominance in the game and expected chances and goals, amount of shots, it’s much higher than what we had last year and we’re on top of things. So it is different, but it’s a draw again.

**on having to focus on finding the back of the net rather than creating more chances:**  
  
I think there’s always a preparation and psychological challenge, because if you’re in a good place, or you’ve won your last game and been successful, you then have to get everyone ready psychologically for the next challenge. You have to get everyone grounded, and in the moment, and that’s no different now. But what’s really important for us is we know we can finish, score goals, we know we have a lot of goalscorers in the squad with a lot of quality, so it’s really important the players know that and they feel our trust with that of course. It’s also about the tactical plan, tweaking small things, and hopefully that makes it easier to create more clear-cut chances.

**on if Baum is ready to play 90 minutes in the WSL:**  
  
Of course, she’ll be able to play 90 minutes, if we look at the wide forward position in the way we play, it’s one of the most demanding positions where there’s a lot of sprinting and high-speed running involved. We have a squad with different qualities, so we can make changes based on different tactical, technical or physical reasons. But she started against Brighton and played around 60 minutes, 75 against Crystal Palace, she’s in a great place, can still improve her repeatability, but she was a really good player for us on the pitch against Crystal Palace.

**on if we talk about statistics much with the squad:**  
  
No, I get the stats now ahead of the press conference - I wasn’t aware of [the unbeaten run] and I don’t think the squad was aware of it. For us, what’s most important is the next game against United and we want to win that game. That’s what we’re focusing on. It’s nice to see in the background, but for us it has no meaning in the moment.

![The WSL unbeaten record we’re looking to set against United](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/large_landscape/3dba1fa6f722-gettyimages-2295173873.webp)

**on how to decide between players who make the squad and those who don’t:**  
  
There’s a lot of different things going into those decisions. One of them is purely physical readiness, it’s readiness from a game model perspective, different scenarios we go through ahead of the game, how we want to start the game and see it play it, how it leads to different scenarios and how we want to finish. So there’s a lot that goes into it, what player qualities we think we need - there are such fine margins going into it at the moment as we have such a great squad and everyone performing at a high level, so those decisions are really difficult. Hindsight is always a beautiful thing, but we try to make high-quality decisions based on as much information as we can, both objectively and subjectively. But it’s difficult, it’s really hard, the hardest part of my job at the moment, and like I said, the squad is capped at 20 - there are bigger squads in the Champions League and a short turnaround, so we’ll need everyone.

**on how Reuteler and Cerci have responded to being left out of the squad:**  
  
They understand the context. Of course they want to represent Arsenal, pull on the shirt and connect with supporters in competitive games, and they will. What we’ve been talking about is the patience and importance of everyone in the squad. It’s a marathon, a long season, and we’re going to need everyone. They’ve been amazing in their response, they are team players, focused on the team, and they’ve been there for the team in the dressing room, around us. So they’ve been real team players, putting themselves aside and being there for the team, which I have so much respect for.

**on if there’s a timeline for Van Domselaar’s return:**At the moment, it's hard to tell. October is in our minds somewhere, but we still have to look at how the new response is. Day by day, there is a plan in place, but that plan has been changed several times now. October will be great, but let's see where it goes. Daphne is working really hard in the background with the medical team.

**on why the WSL is now the most competitive it’s ever been:**Because I think the top teams are of course getting better and better, but everyone else underneath as well, and it's going so explosively. If you look at what clubs are investing, quality of spots, players that are coming to the league, it's really high quality. It's only round two, we're going into round three, so I think it's way too early to draw conclusions yet, but it's highly competitive. We've seen that, we felt that last weekend as well.

**on not being able to predict what’s going to happen:**If it's not fun, but it's easy, there’s no challenge when things are easy. I love it, of course it's challenging, because every single game, everything needs to be top. But like I said, we have a great squad, great staff, everything in a really good place to be able to do that. So no, with the challenge, it comes with some stress, I must admit, but I take joy out of challenges, mostly.

**on if criticism of United has been unfair:**I'm always in favour of kindness in the world, so that would be the starting point. But I also understand the passion of the game and the passion of the supporters. So with that mixture in mind, I do understand that fans want the absolute best for their team. But I think if I look at that situation, the coach has had so little time with the team. So I understand, of course, from a fan perspective, disappointment of results, but I think there's been so little time for them together.

**on what’s slightly different about United now:**You can see on the ball that they do some things differently, which poses different questions to us from a defending perspective. And then the same thing on the other side of the ball, that we think that maybe spaces are a little bit different and behaviours of players on the pitch are a little bit different than what they were before. We see the differences, but I still also see the squad that they have and the players that they have and the foundation that they have. So there will be some sort of hybrid Man United as we knew it and what they are becoming that we expect to face on Saturday.

**on how much these tough games against United, Chelsea and Man City will shape the course of our season:**More games and you're going to play every team twice, once at home and once away. And we have now this first block of the season. We're playing those three opponents all in a row, which, like I just said, I love the challenge. And I think it's good for us that we play those teams early on. We want to take the challenge. We're excited about the challenge. So, no, I look forward to it. Of course, there's a busy schedule coming up for us with the Champions League games in between as well. But I look forward to it. But at the same time, Saturday, United.

![Gallery: Women’s team prepare for Man United](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/xl_landscape/8755878f03c8-z923772i0t8yl2l.webp)

Our 100% start to the 2026/27 season remains intact after we won at the Stadium of Light courtesy of a 2-0 success over Sunderland, as we scrapped hard for our three-point haul.

But why was that the case? Adrian Clarke has run through the data and footage to uncover five key reasons for our 2-0 victory on Wearside:

## STANDING TALL

Regis Le Bris built his game plan around making this contest as physically challenging and hostile as possible, and his Black Cats players followed those orders, with the hosts’ assertive style asking plenty of questions. Pleasingly, we stood firm by grittily pulling together as a collective to keep a fifth clean sheet in six this term.

Ezri Konsa and Gabriel were especially resilient. Taming the threat of muscular striker Brian Brobbey was never easy, but both central defenders made sure they didn't wilt under the duress the Dutchman put on them with his persistent pressing and physicality, standing tall when we needed them to:

Konsa and Gabriel were not alone in this excellent off-the-ball work. In general, our players seemed to relish the hosts’ belligerent approach, matching it with plenty of strength and determination. Winning the majority of the 90 duels contested, it was great to see the team work so hard for one another to keep a highly charged Sunderland outfit at bay:

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/a4531373e690-duels.webp)
![Highlights: Sunderland 0-2 Arsenal](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/large_landscape/d7fd587dac6f-sunderland-england-bruno-guimaraes-of-arsenal-celebrates-scoring-his-teams-first.webp)

## MATCH-WINNING SWITCH

Mikel Arteta replaced Myles Lewis-Skelly with Bruno Guimaraes at half-time, and it proved to be an inspired decision. The midfielder added a little more energy, covering an impressive 6.26km during the second half, just over 1km more than the man he came on for. Statistically, the former Newcastle United skipper also ran with greater intensity too.

Adding more attacking thrust, the Brazilian was also directly involved in both our goals at the Stadium of Light. His first for the club was fiercely struck with precision from 25 yards out.

Seeing that the space was behind him, Guimaraes cleverly backpedalled to create some extra room for himself before receiving Declan Rice’s pass. Then, he caught his shot as sweetly as possible, dipping the ball off the underside of the bar and into the back of the net. It was unstoppable.

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/a7f3cec3691e-bruno3.webp)

Late on, the South American also released Bukayo Saka to win our injury time penalty on Wearside, with a beautiful precision pass. There was very little margin for error, but Guimaraes’ accuracy and weight of pass were flawless to pick out Saka’s intelligent run.

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/1d1238893836-brunopass.webp)

Given his impact on this victory, Guimaraes has put himself into strong contention to make his first league start for us on Saturday at Brighton & Hove Albion.

![Arteta – “It doesn’t get much better than that!”](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/large_landscape/683f0b4e26a2-sunderland-england-bruno-guimaraes-of-arsenal-and-mikel-arteta-manager-of-arsena.webp)

## ANOTHER ACE ODEGAARD DISPLAY

Is there a more in-form attacking midfielder in the division right now than Martin Odegaard? I don’t think so. Our captain is playing superbly, and this was another virtuoso performance from the talented Norwegian.

Five of the 10 chances we created as a team stemmed from Odegaard, who was also denied an assist from this wonderful free-kick delivery for Jurrien Timber, who was narrowly offside:

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/e16f2179945a-timber.webp)

Meanwhile this clever darting run into space inside the box gave Christos Tzolis a nice option for the pass, and Kai Havertz will be disappointed he wasn’t able to convert from Odegaard’s cutback…

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/4a9d4114e522-havchance1.webp)
![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/ed4ae5094f71-havchance1a.webp)

Later in the game, Odegaard also raced forward with the ball at his feet in a 4v2 created by a Tzolis interception, but Saka’s shot from the captain’s well-weight pass was well saved:

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/f9ef89d4fd04-sakasetup.webp)

Odegaard is our creative hub right now. He was excellent again.

## SAKA MOVING INFIELD

Sunderland piled on some pressure in the second period, asserting themselves by bossing an unexpected 53% share of the ball. With their pressing also ferocious, we found it far harder to control the game through quality possession from half-time onwards. This saw us play a little more direct (our long pass proportion rose from 6.7% to 15.5%), with breakaways a more frequent possibility.

Perhaps the biggest tactical change, though, was Saka coming off the right wing to pop up centrally on numerous occasions. In the first half he played in an orthodox right-wing position, but the longer this match went on, the more regularly he showed variety in his movements. Making himself harder to track, Saka got onto the ball down the spine of the pitch a lot more than usual.

The international break is just days away but before the Premier League pauses for an extended period, there's one more gameweek as we head to Brighton & Hove Albion.

We're top of the table going into the weekend with four wins from four matches after an enthralling 2-0 victory over Sunderland last weekend.

Will you be throwing down a chip before the international break? Or perhaps fine-tuning your FPL side before the dust settles.

Regardless of your situation, we're here to give you a helping hand for your line-ups to get the best results in Gameweek 5.

## BEST OF ARSENAL

![Image Widget](https://assets.arsenal.com/prod/images/square_1000_1000/c3ca12362a63-sunderland-england-bukayo-saka-of-arsenal-scores-his-teams-second-goal-from-the.webp)

**David Raya (£6.0m)**was the star of the show in Gameweek 4 as Arsenal continued their 100% start to the Premier League season with a 2-0 victory away at Sunderland. The Gunners number one brilliantly saved a second-half penalty, earning him five FPL points, as well as four clean sheet points and the maximum three bonus points. All in all, Raya returned a whopping 14-point haul and moved to the top of the total points standings for goalkeepers with 29 points. The Spaniard has kept three clean sheets in four matches and is owned by over 40% of Fantasy managers.

In attack, **Bukayo Saka (£9.5m)** continued his brilliant start to the season with his third goal in four matches. The Englishman won and scored a late penalty and is now the Gunners’ highest-scoring player in the game with 30 points. No player had more expected goal involvement (xGI) in the match. Most encouragingly, Saka has played significant minutes in each of the last three Gameweeks. Surprisingly, the Arsenal number seven is still a relative differential, owned by just over 12% of FPL managers. Expect this to rise over the coming Gameweeks.

Elsewhere, **Gabriel (£8.0m)**reminded Fantasy managers why he’s the most expensive defender in the game by scoring nine points at the Stadium of Light. The Brazilian, who has been due to the form of **Riccardo Calafiori (£5.8m)** and the emergence of **Ezri Konsa (£4.5m)**, added two bonus points and defensive contribution points to his clean sheet. Last season, no defender scored more Fantasy points (209) than Gabriel.

The Croatian has notched a goal, two assists and two clean sheets in all.

The Nottingham Forest talisman takes penalties, has high expected minutes and has registered three attacking returns in the last three Gameweeks. Gibbs-White has also claimed maximum bonus points twice.

Brighton duo **Pascal Gross (£5.7m)** and **Maxim De Cuyper (£4.9m)**are proving to be popular purchases after returning 17 and 11-points hauls in the Seagulls’ 5-0 thrashing of Coventry. ### Striker Kaye Furo will be absent for a spell after undergoing an operation on Monday morning, Keith Andrews has confirmed.

#### The 19-year-old, who picked up the Premier League 2 Player of the Month award following impressive performances for Brentford B, was set to start Tuesday night's Carabao Cup round three tie against Reading (8pm kick-off BST, live on *Sky Sports+*).

“[Kaye Furo](http://brentfordfc.com/en/teams/profile/kaye-furo) has picked up an injury in the last few days in training,” Bees head coach [Andrews](https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/teams/profile/keith-andrews) confirmed.

“Unfortunately for him, he’s had to have an operation this [Monday] morning. The timing of an injury is obviously never good for a player, but I felt he was just coming into a really good place with his game.

“That’s really frustrating for him. I would’ve started him against Reading because I felt he deserved it and was in that type of space.

“I’m not sure how long he’s going to be out for but we’ll obviously look after him and get him back to a good place.”

One youngster who will be involved at Select Car Leasing Stadium is centre-back [Benjamin Fredrick](https://www.brentfordfc.com/en/teams/profile/benjamin-fredrick).

On the Nigeria international, who had a loan spell at Belgian Pro League side FCV Dender last term but is yet to make his senior debut for the club, Andrews added: “He hasn’t had a lot of football but has come back in the last couple of weeks.

“We decided not to play him in the B team game on Sunday to make sure he was in the right place to be available for our game against Reading.

“I anticipate he’ll be involved.”

Andrews was also asked about where the domestic cup competitions sit in Brentford's list of priorities this season, and about the test of taking on the League One Royals on Tuesday night.

“We’ve got 5,000 fans going to the game and that, for me, says it all about the belief that fans have that we are taking it very seriously,” he responded.

“It’s a priority, and not just because it’s the next game. We didn’t get to exactly where we wanted to last year, but that’s the plan this year.

“Next up is Reading. We’ll put a team out we feel is right to compete against Reading and, hopefully, get us into the next round.”

# Reading 1 Brentford 2: Carvalho marks comeback with goal as Bees progress to Carabao Cup round four

Fábio Carvalho scores on his return to competitive action as Brentford beat Reading 2-1 to reach round four of the Carabao Cup; Callum Wilson also on target for the Bees at Select Car Leasing Stadium; head coach Keith Andrews: "We had to fight throughout"

Written By

Brentford Football Club

### Fábio Carvalho marked his first competitive appearance in 318 days with a goal as Brentford defeated Reading 2-1 to progress to round four of the Carabao Cup.

#### Callum Wilson opened the scoring inside three minutes before Carvalho doubled the Bees’ advantage in first-half stoppage time. Paudie O’Connor pulled one back for Reading after the break, but Keith Andrews’ side held firm at Select Car Leasing Stadium.

The Bees boss made eight changes to his starting XI. Among those coming into the side was [Carvalho](/en/teams/mens/fabio-carvalho), who was involved in a competitive fixture for the first time since Brentford’s trip to Crystal Palace on 1 November 2025.

The midfielder was subsequently sidelined with an anterior cruciate ligament injury before returning to action with the B team and featuring for the first team against Rennes in pre-season.

Goalkeeper Ellery Balcombe made his second senior appearance for the club, while summer signing El Hadji Malick Diouf started for the first time**.**

Brentford took the lead inside three minutes. Carvalho fed Dango Ouattara down the right and, when he slipped while attempting to collect the return pass, the ball ran through to [Wilson](/en/teams/mens/callum-wilson). The striker swept a composed finish into the bottom corner from 12 yards.

Rico Henry, partnering Kristoffer Ajer in central defence, made an important intervention, cutting out Josh Stokes’ through ball before Randell Williams could latch on to it.

The Royals had the ball in the net on 12 minutes through Paudie O’Connor’s acrobatic finish, but the referee ruled it out for a high foot.

O’Connor then headed Charlie Savage’s free-kick from the left onto the roof of the net, while Diouf’s long-range effort at the opposite end flew over the crossbar.

Midway through the half, Randell Williams worked the ball into the box and Balcombe made a sprawling save to deny Jamie Reid.

Reading kept the attack alive. Williams’ deflected cross travelled towards the back post, where Reid slipped as he attempted to meet it, and the ball bounced behind for a goal-kick.

Damsgaard’s cross from the right was flicked on by Wilson and Keane Lewis-Potter met it with a fierce strike, forcing Joel Pereira to launch himself to his right and push the ball behind for a corner.

Diouf sent the ball up the channel and O’Connor’s slip presented Wilson with a sight of goal, but the striker could not generate enough power to trouble Pereira, who gathered his shot comfortably.

Lewis-Potter then teed up Carvalho on the edge of the box, but his shot was blocked by a Reading defender.

Henry produced another vital intervention on 45 minutes, racing back to poke the ball away from Reid as the forward closed in on goal. From the resulting corner, Conor Masterson glanced Savage’s in-swinging delivery narrowly wide**.**

Brentford doubled their lead in the final seconds before the break. Ouattara played a defence-splitting pass that Wilson cleverly dummied, allowing the ball to run into Carvalho’s path. The midfielder took a touch to set himself before calmly slotting home.

110

Shortly after the restart, Brentford moved the ball from left to right across the face of Reading’s penalty area. Ouattara received a pass from Wilson and drove narrowly wide from 10 yards.

Balcombe got down quickly to smother Josh Stokes’ shot after the ball broke to him in the Bees’ box.

Andrews’ side came close to adding a third on 63 minutes. Henry clipped a first-time cross towards the back post, where Ouattara’s header was clawed away by Pereira. Kayode then fired into the side netting from close range.

Ouattara then threatened again, heading Kayode’s cross just over the bar.

Reading reduced the deficit on 72 minutes. Ajer bravely blocked Stokes’ goal-bound effort, but O’Connor nodded home from Savage’s resulting corner.

Kayode’s cross bounced through to substitute Igor Thiago as the Bees looked to restore their two-goal advantage, but the striker failed to make clean contact and Pereira gathered comfortably.

Thiago turned provider moments later, teeing up Damsgaard on the edge of the box, but the Dane skewed his effort high and wide.

Thiago latched on to Lewis-Potter’s ball over the top and held off Jeriel Dorsett, but Pereira raced off his line to narrow the angle and deny the striker.

Jannik Schuster headed in a corner in the final seconds, but the referee disallowed the goal for a foul.

Brentford will find out their next Carabao Cup opponents following the conclusion of the televised tie between Manchester United and Brighton and Hove Albion on Wednesday night.

**Reading:** Pereira; Ahmed, Masterson, O'Connor (Dorsett 79), Roberts (Lane 63); Savage, Fraser; Williams, Stokes (Earthy 88), Kyerewaa (Lisbie 79); Reid (Brown 63)

**Subs:** Stevens, Godwin-Malife, Wing, Beacroft

**Brentford:** Balcombe; Kayode, Ajer, Henry, Diouf (Schuster 61); Ouattara (Anthony 77), Damsgaard, Sangaré (Yarmoliuk HT), Lewis-Potter; Carvalho (Hickey 77), Wilson (Thiago 77)

**Subs:** Kelleher, Fredrick, Janelt, Schade

**Attendance:** 13,489 (4,992)

### Andrews: We had to fight throughout

[![Placeholder Image](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fopen.http.mp.streamamg.com%2Fp%2F3001557%2Fsp%2F300155700%2Fthumbnail%2Fentry_id%2F0_1hfx7x8o%2Fwidth%2F900&w=1920&q=75)

02:31](#)

##### Reaction: Keith Andrews post-Reading

**Reflecting on the victory, Keith Andrews was pleased with much of his side’s performance, particularly given the number of changes to his starting XI.**

“I’m pleased with a lot of it,” he said. “As everyone will be fully aware, that team hasn’t played together before, so not everything was going to be cohesive at times. We had a couple of square pegs in round holes.

“But, with the personnel we had on the pitch, we felt confident we’d get a performance. At times we looked very, very good; at times it looked like a team that hadn’t played together much.”

The Brentford head coach also praised Reading’s display and the challenge they posed his side.

“We had to fight throughout,” Andrews added. “They were excellent and caused us a lot of problems.”

### Return to first-team action 'a blessing', says Carvalho

[![Placeholder Image](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fopen.http.mp.streamamg.com%2Fp%2F3001557%2Fsp%2F300155700%2Fthumbnail%2Fentry_id%2F0_zopcrieq%2Fwidth%2F900&w=1920&q=75)

02:10](#)

##### Reaction: Fábio Carvalho post-Reading

**Fábio Carvalho described his return to action as “a blessing” after scoring in Brentford’s 2-1 Carabao Cup win.**

“It was amazing,” he said. “It was just a blessing. It’s been a long, hard few months, but I was happy to be out there.

“I was happy to be out there in front of our 5,000 fans, which was amazing. They kept pushing us, kept supporting us and they’ve just been amazing. Credit to them again for coming out here today; we’re just grateful.”

Carvalho was also pleased to mark his return with a goal just before half-time: “Before I scored, I was thinking, ‘We need another goal here’, because they were trying to get back into the game.

“For them, at home, it was a big, big game, but it came at the right time.”

results.title: Xabi Alonso confirms Chelsea team news for Brentford
results.raw_content:
Xabi Alonso confirmed that Joao Pedro and Reece James, along with the whole of his Chelsea squad, remain in contention to face Brentford going into matchday.

The Blues make the short trip across west London to take on Brentford in the Premier League’s Friday night kick-off, hoping to get back to winning ways after last week’s 2-2 draw with Hull City at Stamford Bridge.

There were concerns over [Joao Pedro](/en/teams/profile/joao-pedro) after the striker withdrew from the Brazil squad for the upcoming international break, and James as he missed the start of training on Tuesday. However, Alonso insists they have not been ruled out of our next match.

‘In terms of injuries and in terms of the squad we are having the last training session tomorrow so no-one is ruled out for us for Friday,’ he explained.

‘So I prefer to be cautious and we will wait until tomorrow to take the final decision on every player. We will see tomorrow if Joao is ready to play, it’s a possibility.

‘For Reece, it was just a decision for Tuesday and we see his development and tomorrow we will decide.’

Our manager also hinted that there is a chance that [Moises Caicedo](/en/teams/profile/moises-caicedo) could return to the matchday squad, with the midfielder having been restricted to just a brief appearance against Brighton & Hove Albion so far this season.

‘He’s getting closer and tomorrow we will take the final decision on the team and on the squad that is coming to Brentford.’

It was a similar response when Alonso was asked in his pre-match press conference if [Marco Palestra](/en/teams/profile/marco-palestra) or [Jordan Henderson](/en/teams/profile/jordan-henderson) could be fit enough to make their Chelsea debuts at the Gtech Community Stadium, underlining that he will continue to monitor his options right up until it comes to the moment to name his team on Friday.

‘Tomorrow is the final decision,' he added. 'Sorry to repeat myself, but before the players know we need to assess all the positions with the last training and tomorrow we will make the decision for the game in Brentford.’

results.title: Brentford vs Chelsea: All you need to know | News
results.raw_content:
Chelsea’s localised start to the season on all fronts continues with a seventh match in succession played in the capital. Club historian Rick Glanvill and club statistician Paul Dutton preview our trip to Brentford’s Gtech Community Stadium.

The 8pm Friday kick-off will also be the Blues’ last west London derby on the road of the current league campaign.

End-to-end 2-2 draws at the weekend prompted both managers to wistfully wish for a ‘boring’ game – 51 goals have already been scored in matches across all competitions involving the west London pair.

The unbeaten Bees have drawn three on the spin in the top flight, but won 2-1 at Reading in midweek to reach the last 16 of the Carabao Cup. Chelsea's ball was already in the round four bowl so Xabi Alonso had a free week to prepare his players for this fixture after Saturday’s 2-2 home draw with Hull.

Alonso and Keith Andrews will lock horns in the technical area for the first time, but at Euro 2012 they vied for midfield supremacy as Spain beat the Republic of Ireland 4-0, a win in which Chelsea’s Fernando Torres scored twice.

In this same fixture last season at the Gtech, the Blues came from behind to lead, but conceded a last-gasp equaliser for 2-2 and a share of the spoils.

Either club claiming all three points would lift them to third place in the table going into the weekend action. After that comes FIFA’s three-week, four-match international break, with club football resuming on 10 October, when Chelsea host Bournemouth.

## Team news

Alonso confirmed that [Joao Pedro](/en/teams/profile/joao-pedro) and [Reece James](/en/teams/profile/reece-james), along with the whole of his Chelsea squad, remain in contention to face Brentford. There were concerns over [Joao Pedro](/en/teams/profile/joao-pedro) after the striker withdrew from the Brazil squad for the upcoming international break, and James as he missed the start of training on Tuesday.

‘In terms of injuries and in terms of the squad, we are having the last training session on Friday so no-one is ruled out for us,’ he explained in his pre-match press conference.

‘So I prefer to be cautious and we will wait to take the final decision on every player. We will see if Joao is ready to play, it’s a possibility. For Reece, it was just a decision for Tuesday and we see his development and we will decide.’

It was a similar story when Alonso discussed the potential return from injury of [Moises Caicedo](/en/teams/profile/moises-caicedo), [Marco Palestra](/en/teams/profile/marco-palestra) and [Jordan Henderson](/en/teams/profile/jordan-henderson).

‘Moises is getting closer and we will take the final decision on the team and on the squad that is coming to Brentford. Before the players know we need to assess all the positions with the last training and we will make the decision for the game.’

## The history

One of Chelsea’s most memorable trips to Maine Road came in a rare Friday night match in early May 1984, Match Of The Day coverage of the tussle with Manchester City vying with That’s My Boy on ITV for the viewing public’s attention. It was the first time a Division Two match had been given the BBC’s live treatment and already-promoted Chelsea struck twice in six minutes to show why they and not the Cityzens were rejoining the elite.

Fast forward eight years to 11 December 1992 and a dour 0-0 between Middlesbrough and Chelsea meant Teesside hosted the first Friday night match in Premier League history.

The August 2002 clash between the Blues and Manchester United at Stamford Bridge was brought forward to the end of the working week to avoid Notting Hill Carnival congestion. The hosts twice led though William Gallas then Boudewijn Zenden, but the Mancunians levelled on each occasion and an entertaining game finished 2-2.

Friday 12 May 2017 at West Bromwich Albion proved a red letter day in the Black Country for the Blues. The hosts doggedly held out until Michy Batshuayi’s opportunistic winner and at the final whistle the title-winning celebrations were lengthy and joyful.

Last season, the same night of the week served up substantial away wins on two fronts – 5-1 at West Ham United in the league and 4-0 at Hull City in the FA Cup. Those were the Blues’ second and third-highest scores of the season and [Pedro Neto](/en/teams/profile/pedro-neto) notched four across the two games.

Prior to that, a Marc Cucurella goal without reply had claimed all three points at home to Man Utd in May 2025, making the 3-0 at Brighton & Hove Albion two months earlier our most recent Friday loss.

## Know this...

No Premier League goalkeeper has made more saves this season than Chelsea’s Emi Martinez or Brentford’s Caoimhin Kelleher (both 15).

The Blues have recorded and sustained the joint-most shots on target in the top flight, 24 for and 26 against.

Chelsea have broken the deadlock in the opening seven minutes of all four Premier League fixtures to date – in the first minute at Fulham, fourth at home to Brighton, second at Arsenal and seventh against Hull.

Last weekend, [Cole Palmer](/en/teams/profile/cole-palmer) marked his 100th Premier League appearance with his 71st goal contribution (49 goals, 22 assists). Only Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink produced more in his first century for the Blues.

Joao Pedro has already set up and scored a goal in the same top-flight game three times this season, matching his best performance in any campaign in England.

The Bees have opened the scoring in each of their past three league games, and conceded the equaliser on each occasion.

results.title: Alonso confident there's 'more to come' from Cole Palmer
results.raw_content:
Cole Palmer has started the season in excellent form and Xabi Alonso believes our No10 can reach even greater heights if he keeps enjoying his football.

Palmer was outstanding in his first two campaigns at Stamford Bridge, but injury made it difficult for him to replicate that level of performance in 2025/26.

He didn’t go to the FIFA World Cup this summer, and the break afforded him a chance to rest and reset. It has served Palmer well, with the attacker already finding the net four times and registering two assists.

We will find out today if Palmer is back in the England fold, but for now Alonso has urged him to just keep playing with a smile on his face.

‘I think there's some more to come from Cole,’ said Alonso.

‘I'm very happy with Cole. The way he has prepared since the first day of pre-season, he's been there. He has shown this desire to enjoy his game.

‘What he wants is to enjoy his game, to have this good feeling on the pitch, to have this connection with players around. If he gets that, the rest will come. England will come, winning more games will come.

‘That will come naturally because he's a top-level player and that's the main thing, for him to feel good.’

Alonso has not been working with Palmer for long, but he can already tell he has a unique personality that will continue to stand him in good stead.

‘I've been here for two months. Day by day I get to know the players better, and I get to know Cole better, and Cole gets to know me better.

‘It’s about having connection, having contact, and Cole is a special man.’

results.title: Bompastor on James' new role and Potter's deserved ...
results.raw_content:
Following Chelsea Women’s brilliant 5-0 win over Manchester United, head coach Sonia Bompastor highlighted the performances of Lauren James and Lexi Potter.

Bompastor made two changes to her line-up as we took the trip to Manchester looking for our first Women’s Super League win of the season, having been held to a 1-1 draw at Stamford Bridge by Aston Villa in our opening game.

With [Aggie Beever-Jones](/en/teams/profile/aggie-beever-jones) among the substitutes this time around, those changes saw James switching to a central striker’s role. It produced the desired results as the England international netted our third goal of a resounding victory over the Red Devils.

‘I think we all know LJ is probably not a real number nine and she likes to drop deep and have the ball,’ said Bompastor, after seeing her team pick up our first league win of the campaign in emphatic fashion.

‘So it's important when we play with LJ as a number nine to have two number tens who are in the pocket, but also making penetrating runs. That's why it's important for us to pay attention when we decide which profiles are playing around her.

‘It’s important to have this threat because I think on Sunday we could exploit the space behind the back line for United and we were quite good at doing that.’

The player who came into the line-up in place of Beever-Jones was Academy graduate Potter, the 20-year-old taking her spot in midfield for her first WSL start of the season, after impressing in the 1-0 UEFA Women’s Champions League win away at Real Sociedad.

‘I already said I am a manager who really likes to develop young players,’ Bompastor continued.

‘I want to give them the opportunity when they have the right mindset, they work hard and they have the quality. I'm always keen to do that.

‘Lexi deserves to get minutes in this team. She's a really good player. Sometimes it depends on the tactics, the different profiles we want to use and the different systems we are playing.

‘But it was a good opportunity for her and she had a good performance. That's the best thing she can do for me to keep her on the pitch.’

results.title: How Chelsea reversed scoring fortunes with emphatic Man ...
results.raw_content:
Chelsea responded in style to the disappointing 1-1 draw with Aston Villa on the opening day of the Women's Super League season by putting five goals past Manchester United away from home without reply.

Against Villa, the Blues had created plenty, firing 35 shots towards the opposition's goal, with the data revealing we created an xG (Expected Goals) rating of 3.6. Yet we found the back of the net just once, and a late equaliser from the visitors meant we came away with just one point to show from such a dominant display.

After the match, head coach [Sonia Bompastor](/en/teams/profile/sonia-bompastor) explained why clinical finishing is so important. 'The reality of football is that in this kind of game, we need to be two or three-nil up by half-time, and the game is over,' she said in her post-match press conference. 'Then, it's a completely different game coming into the second half because when you have two or three goals difference, you can bring players in, rotate the squad.'

Her words acted as a prophecy of sorts as the Blues raced into a 2-0 lead by half-time against Manchester United thanks to goals from [Sjoeke Nusken](/en/teams/profile/sjoeke-nusken) and [Keira Walsh](/en/teams/profile/keira-walsh). [Lauren James](/en/teams/profile/lauren-james-19) promptly added a third on the hour mark.

True to what she explained the previous week, Bompastor made a triple substitution in the 71st minute, rotating James, [Katie McCabe](/en/teams/profile/katie-mccabe) and [Alyssa Thompson](/en/teams/profile/alyssa-thompson) for [Sandy Baltimore](/en/teams/profile/sandy-baltimore), [Veerle Buurman](/en/teams/profile/veerle-buurman) and [Maika Hamano](/en/teams/profile/maika-hamano), before goals from [Ellie Carpenter](/en/teams/profile/ellie-carpenter) and [Lucy Bronze](/en/teams/profile/lucy-bronze) completed the rout. Here's a look at how we turned our fortunes around.

## Clinical Blues

Against Villa, we created enough chances to produce an xG rating of 3.6, but netted only once. In contrast, we produced a rating of 2.94 against Manchester United but outscored that number with five goals on the day.

After the match, [Wieke Kaptein](/en/teams/profile/wieke-kaptein) explained that the Blues had been working on crossing through the week in training, and that approach certainly paid off.

The stats reveal that clinical finishing made the difference against the Red Devils, as we scored five times from 25 shots on goal and 30 crosses. Against Villa, we scored once from ten more shots (35) and 11 more crosses (41), showing that quality over quantity was key to our success at the Progress With Unity Stadium.

## Dominating the opposition

Keen to ensure we took all three points away from Manchester, Bompastor played an aggressive formation. Katie McCabe and Lucy Bronze pushed up high, leaving just [Kadeisha Buchanan](/en/teams/profile/kadeisha-buchanan) from the back three to stay deep and alert to the danger of counter-attacks.

McCabe and Bronze supported a double-pivot midfield made up of [Lexi Potter](/en/teams/profile/lexi-potter) and Keira Walsh, while we went for an all-out attack with a front five of Ellie Carpenter, Kaptein, James, Nusken and Alyssa Thompson.

Meanwhile, Manchester United were playing only their second match under new boss Eva Olid since parting ways with longstanding head coach Marc Skinner in the summer.

Bompastor's ruthless approach gave a side attempting to implement a new style of play no choice but to retreat backwards to deal with the constant goal threats from our talented front five, as the graphic below shows. The home side were reduced to an xG of 0.20, attempting just two shots on goal and taking only four touches in our box.

Our all-out attacking approach may not be the correct solution for every match, but on Sunday it worked perfectly. Not only did we secure all three points, but the performance will have undoubtedly boosted the team's confidence in the shooting department.

## Unsung hero Kaptein

While Kaptein was not among the scorers on Sunday, her determined performance was crucial to the win. Unselfishly working to make the attack click, the Netherlands international created the most chances of anyone during the afternoon (four), and also regained possession more than any other Chelsea player, winning the ball back on ten separate occasions.

Her tenacity allowed us to keep up the relentless pressure up front, also winning three aerial duels and making 24 passes in the final third of the pitch.   
  
‘We kept possession a little bit longer, saw where the spaces were,' Kaptein said afterwards. 'Then I think a lot of people were in front of the goal, which was really good. So every time they came across or when there was an opportunity, I think everyone was ready for it.'

## Walsh shines going forward

Usually known for her elite skills in the holding midfield role, Keira Walsh made a strong display in attack during what was her 50th appearance for Chelsea in our 5-0 win on Sunday.

Scoring with a beautifully-struck effort from outside the box to put us two goals in front, Walsh also assisted James after 61 minutes and won the Player of the Match trophy for her performance. The heat map below shows how she got forward into shooting range, in particular the right-hand side of the final third.

Ordinarily, if Walsh were to make forward runs like those indicated on the heat map, she would be leaving a gaping hole in front of the defence. Yet the experienced England international was free to advance, thanks to her midfield partner and Chelsea Academy graduate Lexi Potter.

The 20-year-old had the highest pass completion rate of the entire team (91.7 per cent from 48 attempts), showing that she was careful with the ball and executed her role in the system perfectly.

‘Lexi deserves to get minutes in this team,' said Bompastor afterwards. 'She's a really good player. Sometimes it depends on the tactics, the different profiles we want to use and the different systems we are playing. But it was a good opportunity for her, and she had a good performance.'

On this occasion, our head coach trusted Potter to keep the ball moving, without losing possession in dangerous areas. She did exactly that, which in turn allowed her midfield partner Walsh to have so much success in attack.

# Team News: Sage hints at possible Sarr & Nketiah returns

## [First-team](/news/first-team/)

Pierre Sage says Ismaïla Sarr and Eddie Nketiah could both return to the matchday squad for Crystal Palace’s first-ever UEFA Europa League fixture on Thursday.

The Eagles will host Polish champions Lech Poznań on Thursday evening at Selhurst Park (20:00 BST) – [with tickets available here](https://www.eticketing.co.uk/cpfc/Events?utm_source=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=WebStoryTickets100926) – and could be bolstered by the return of two attackers for our league phase opener.

Last season’s top scorer Sarr has yet to feature competitively so far this season, whilst Nketiah started our first three games of the season, but missed Palace’s two home fixtures last week.

Sage said of **Sarr**: “He could be in the team tomorrow, as [could] **Eddie Nketiah**, because they started to train with us this week, and they are in shape.”

Asked further about **Jean-Philippe Mateta** and **Dean Henderson** – the former missing since the opening day of the season, the latter also absent from last week’s matches, Sage said of the duo’s returns: “I hope it will be after the international break.

“With long injuries, there’s more or less days. That’s why we hope and we will see.”

Although he will be absent on Thursday, it was announced just before the press conference that Henderson has signed a new contract with the club, committing his future to Palace until 2030.

Sage smiled: “We are really happy for us, we are really happy for him – it’s a long-term contract for our captain.

“For the moment he is injured, but he showed us during his first games that he’s really important for the team and we hope he’ll come back quickly, because he’s really important in the dressing room too. That’s why this kind of news is good news for us.

“As a player, he’s a really good goalkeeper, and as a man he has good leadership, he’s positive, and he’s always with his teammates, that’s why it’s really important to have him.

“But we have to consider him with the other goalkeepers too, because they do a good job altogether. If Dean's level is high, it’s because his teammates’ is too.”

# Report: Eagles ease past Poznan in excellent Europa debut

[Match reports](/news/match-reports/)

4

Strand Larsen 34'

Richards 27'

Pino 10'

0

Crystal Palace ran rampant on their UEFA Europa League debut, cruising past Polish league champions Lech Poznań 4-0 at Selhurst Park to record their biggest-ever European win.

Pierre Sage’s Eagles were on top from the off, Yéremy Pino a constant menace in the opening stages – and duly capitalising on a terrible throw-in from Terry Yegbe to nip in front of his man and prod past the onrushing goalkeeper.

Poznan did briefly rally, but Palace were simply too good and continued to scythe through, Chris Richards doubling our advantage from a corner-kick not long before the 30-minute mark – before Pino won a penalty which Jørgen Strand Larsen swept home.

Palace enjoyed further chances to extend their lead in the second-half – with Poznań reduced to 10 men late on – and duly took one with two minutes remaining, Eddie Nketiah coming off the bench to open his account for 2026/27 and Dwight McNeil providing his first assist.

Overall, Palace could take pride in an exemplary Europa League debut which saw them sit second in the league phase table – behind only Juventus – at the full-time whistle.

### Summary:

* Eagles unchanged from the weekend for Europa League debut.
* 5: Exciting opening sees both teams trade early chances, as Pino tests Lis.
* 10 – GOAL: Pino pounces on a loose throw-in and finishes clinically.
* 22: Ishak volleys over after Rodriguez lobs over the top towards him.
* 25: Yegbe volleys wide at the conclusion of a clever set-piece.
* 27 – GOAL: Richards rises highest to double the Eagles’ advantage
* 34 – GOAL: Pino wins a penalty and Strand Larsen smashes home to put Palace in dreamland.
* 36: Yegbe converts into his own net from long range in comical fashion – but Strand Larsen is inches offside in the build-up.
* **HT: Palace 3-0 Lech Poznań**
* 52: Kamada flashes in an inviting cross but Strand Larsen can’t make clean contact.
* 55: Palma tests Benítez’s handling low down at his near post.
* 66: Pino’s effort deflects over at the end of another fantastic move by the Eagles.
* 74: Sarr returns to action off the bench.
* 76: Nketiah is played through by Pino on the stretch, but skews his effort wide.
* 82: Benítez makes an excellent stop low down to deny Gurgul a late consolation.
* 87 - RED CARD: Murawski is dismissed for a second yellow card.
* 89 - GOAL: Nketiah adds further gloss to the scoreline with a late finish.
* **FT: Palace 4-0 Lech Poznań**

So here it was. UEFA Europa League football at Selhurst Park… some would say, at last.

Off the back of a frustrating late defeat to Ipswich in SE25 days before, despite a promising performance in spells, Sage picked an unchanged side, with Adam Wharton once again skippering the side in the absence of Dean Henderson.

Both teams’ matches so far this season had seen an onrush of goals – 12 of Palace’s last 14 competitive matches had produced at least three of them, whilst seven of Lech Poznan’s last eight games saw three or more.

Fittingly, there were early chances at both ends – as both centre-forwards failed to make the cleanliness of touch they would have liked.

First, Mikael Ishak – Ismaïla Sarr’s nearest rival for the UEFA Conference League golden boot last season – narrowly missed Patrik Walemark’s ball across the box. Then, up the other end, a bouncing ball dropped invitingly for Jørgen Strand Larsen, but his swipe took it away from goal.

The early pace persisted. Seconds later, Yéremy Pino linked up with in-form creator Daichi Kamada, danced past one defender and bent it towards the far stick. A deflection took it the opposite direction – but Mateusz Lis reacted well in the Poznan goal to turn it away.

Moments later, Pino cut inside from the same left-hand side and bent one over the bar. He was in red-hot form… and on the 10-minute mark, showed it.

With Terry Yegbe lining up to throw the ball long down the touchline, the Poznan defender had a momentary lapse of judgment, shifting his body and launching it square – into no man’s land.

Pino still had plenty to do, but did it superbly, prodding the ball past his trailing defender and then lifting it delightfully over Lis to get Palace off the mark just 10 minutes into Europa League life.

Palace continued to pour plenty of bodies forwards and looked the more likely to double their lead, but Poznań did give a hint at their goalscoring pedigree when Ishak volleyed over from Pablo Rodriguez’s chipped pass over the top, and Yegbe – seeking redemption – touched wide from close-range after a clever set-piece routine involving Allahyar Sayyadmanesh.

Nevertheless, it seemed like only a matter of time until Palace doubled their lead.

And so they did on 27 minutes with a simple goal: more intricate passing yielded a corner which Wharton swung towards the back post, and which Chris Richards crashed home a header – despite the presence of several Poznań bodies on their line.

It would get even better moments later, thanks to the unplayable Pino. The Spaniard drifted in from the left again and chopped it back between his legs, before being fouled inside the box.

Up stepped his good friend Jørgen Strand Larsen to win a penalty – crashing the ball into the top corner, with Lis diving the other way, for his fourth goal in three games.

Selhurst could barely believe its eyes – and it could have been even better two minutes later following another comical mix-up involving Lis and Yegbe, the latter – panicked by Strand Larsen’s presence – turning into his own net from 30 yards. The Palace man, this time, was narrowly offside.

When the half-time whistle sounded, there was no doubt – in the Europa League, Palace had arrived.

The second-half, as is so often the way in such matches, became more about managing the occasion, although Kamada did have one particularly fine delivery flicked wide by Strand Larsen, who perhaps ought to have done better in the moment.

Luis Palma had a fierce shot low down towards Walter Benítez’s near post – the Palace ‘keeper claiming confidently – but the Eagles were seeing more of the ball, more of the chances, and most certainly more of the play.

A raft of substitutions from both sides slowed down the pace of the play – but Palace always looked capable of going up a gear.

A magnificent move on 66 minutes evidenced that as Pino nodded down for Wharton, who sprayed a lovely half-volley into the path of Tyrick Mitchell. He duly slipped in substitute Dwight McNeil, who back-heeled towards Pino – and the finish, the last part of a delightful move, was blocked on the slide, when it deserved a goal.

In full control, Palace could have added more, Wharton with a low drive wide and Eddie Nketiah – making his return from injury off the bench along with Ismaïla Sarr – screwing a strike wide when played through on goal by Pino.

Poznań had a late chance too as Michal Gurgul hit a firm first-time drive which Benítez did brilliantly to beat away, low to his left.

But the visitors failed to finish the match with a full complement of players, experienced defender Radoslaw Murawski picking up a needless second yellow card late on.

And Nketiah put the seal on the night by capitalising two minutes later. McNeil spun wonderfully in midfield and slipped in the No. 9 with an inch-perfect pass, and he chopped back onto his weaker left foot before sliding it beyond Lis for the Eagles' fourth of a glorious night.

On their way... to Frankfurt? A lot of football to be played before then, for sure, but an early indicator of Palace's intentions in this competition.

On the evidence of this performance, you wouldn't bet against it.

**Palace:** Benítez (GK), Ahanor, Richards (Canvot, 73), Disasi, Khalaili (Mingueza, 61), Timber (McNeil, 62), Wharton, Mitchell, Pino, Kamada (Sarr, 74), Strand Larsen (Nketiah, 74).
